\chapter{Right, Wrong, Maybe}
\label{ch:te-right-wrong-maybe}
\hlchaptermodality{87}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say that something is wrong or exactly right, answer with maybe, and react with really? and I see.}

Complete TE-R87-second-pass-replies: the chapter replies and the requests that keep a conversation going, from cold.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[tappu]{\te{తప్పు} (tappu) — a mistake; wrong}

\label{lesson:TE-C87-mistake}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for one minute, then the Telugu for please wait.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{తప్పు}}
\textbf{\te{తప్పు}} (\emph{tappu}) — \textquotedblleft{}a mistake\textquotedblright{}, and as a reply, \textquotedblleft{}wrong\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{క్షమించండి}, \te{నా} \te{తప్పు}} — \textquotedblleft{}sorry, my mistake\textquotedblright{}.

You have met it before without seeing it: \textbf{\te{తప్పకుండా}}, \textquotedblleft{}certainly\textquotedblright{}, is built on the verb behind this word, \textquotedblleft{}to slip, to miss\textquotedblright{}. Certainly is \emph{without slipping}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A word for a mistake, and the word for certainly finally explained.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tappu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tappu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{kṣamin̄caṇḍi, nā tappu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for one minute, then the Telugu for please wait, then say \emph{tappu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{తప్పు} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A mistake; wrong\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[sariggā]{\te{సరిగ్గా} (sariggā) — exactly, properly}

\label{lesson:TE-C87-exactly}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for please wait, then the Telugu for a mistake.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{సరిగ్గా}}
\textbf{\te{సరిగ్గా}} (\emph{sariggā}) — \textquotedblleft{}exactly, properly\textquotedblright{}.

Said alone, \textbf{\te{సరిగ్గా}!} is \textquotedblleft{}exactly!\textquotedblright{}. It shares its start with \textbf{\te{సరే}}, \textquotedblleft{}okay\textquotedblright{}: both lean on \textbf{\te{సరి}}, \textquotedblleft{}right, even\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Wrong and exactly right, as a pair.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sariggā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sariggā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{sariggā!} to agree strongly
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for please wait, then the Telugu for a mistake, then say \emph{sariggā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{సరిగ్గా} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Exactly, properly\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bahuśā]{\te{బహుశా} (bahuśā) — probably, perhaps}

\label{lesson:TE-C87-probably}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for a mistake, then the Telugu for exactly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{బహుశా}}
\textbf{\te{బహుశా}} (\emph{bahuśā}) — \textquotedblleft{}probably, perhaps\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{బహుశా} \te{రేపు}} — \textquotedblleft{}probably tomorrow\textquotedblright{}. Compare \textbf{\te{ఏమో}}: \emph{ēmō} shrugs, \textquotedblleft{}who knows\textquotedblright{}, while \emph{bahuśā} makes a guess.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A guess, next to the shrug you already had.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bahuśā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bahuśā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{bahuśā rēpu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for a mistake, then the Telugu for exactly, then say \emph{bahuśā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{బహుశా} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Probably, perhaps\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[alāgā]{\te{అలాగా} (alāgā) — is that so? I see}

\label{lesson:TE-C87-isee}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for exactly, then the Telugu for probably.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{అలాగా}}
\textbf{\te{అలాగా}} (\emph{alāgā}) — \textquotedblleft{}is that so?\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}I see\textquotedblright{}.

It sits one vowel away from \textbf{\te{అలాగే}}, \textquotedblleft{}alright then\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Alāgā} receives news; \emph{alāgē} agrees to a plan. Say both and hear the difference in the last vowel.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A way to show you are listening.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{alāgā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{alāgā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{alāgā}, then \emph{alāgē}, and hear the last vowel change
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for exactly, then the Telugu for probably, then say \emph{alāgā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{అలాగా} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Is that so? I see\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[nijaṁgā]{\te{నిజంగా} (nijaṁgā) — really, truly}

\label{lesson:TE-C87-really}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for probably, then the Telugu for I see.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{నిజంగా}}
\textbf{\te{నిజంగా}} (\emph{nijaṁgā}) — \textquotedblleft{}really, truly\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{నిజం}} is \textquotedblleft{}the truth\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{-\te{గా}} turns it into a manner, as it did for \emph{nemmadigā}. As a question, \textbf{\te{నిజంగా}?} is \textquotedblleft{}really?\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Five replies: wrong, exactly, probably, I see, really.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nijaṁgā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nijaṁgā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nijaṁgā?} with a rising voice
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for probably, then the Telugu for I see, then say \emph{nijaṁgā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{నిజంగా} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Really, truly\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Keeping a conversation going — a second pass}

\label{lesson:TE-R87-second-pass-replies}



\begin{quote}
Someone speaks fast and quietly. Ask for three things: slowly, louder, once more.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: the ending -\te{గా}}]
\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{word} & \textbf{built from} \\
\midrule
\textbf{\te{నెమ్మదిగా}} & slow + -\te{గా} \\
\textbf{\te{గట్టిగా}} & firm + -\te{గా} \\
\textbf{\te{సరిగ్గా}} & right + -\te{గా} \\
\textbf{\te{నిజంగా}} & truth + -\te{గా} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

One ending, four manners. It is the same \textbf{-\te{గా}} that made \emph{nāku caligā undi}.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item ask someone to wait one minute
  \item you made a mistake; say sorry and own it
  \item agree strongly, then guess \textquotedblleft{}probably tomorrow\textquotedblright{}
  \item react to news with \textquotedblleft{}I see\textquotedblright{}, then with \textquotedblleft{}really?\textquotedblright{}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Slowly? (\textbf{\te{నెమ్మదిగా}}.) Once more? (\textbf{\te{ఇంకోసారి}}.) Louder? (\textbf{\te{గట్టిగా}}.) One minute? (\textbf{\te{ఒక్క} \te{నిమిషం}}.) Please wait? (\textbf{\te{ఆగండి}}.) My mistake? (\textbf{\te{నా} \te{తప్పు}}.) Exactly? (\textbf{\te{సరిగ్గా}}.) Probably? (\textbf{\te{బహుశా}}.) I see? (\textbf{\te{అలాగా}}.) Really? (\textbf{\te{నిజంగా}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{How are you, honestly — a second pass}

\label{lesson:TE-R87-second-pass-feelings}



\begin{quote}
You are not well today. Say that you have a fever, that your head aches, and that you are tired.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: two ways a feeling reaches you}]
\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{it comes to you} & \textbf{it is so, to you} \\
\midrule
\textbf{\te{నాకు} \te{జ్వరం} \te{వచ్చింది}} & \textbf{\te{నాకు} \te{అలసటగా} \te{ఉంది}} \\
\textbf{\te{నాకు} \te{కోపం} \te{వచ్చింది}} & \textbf{\te{నాకు} \te{భయంగా} \te{ఉంది}} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

Both keep the person in the dative \textbf{\te{నాకు}}. One says the thing arrived; the other says how it is with you now. \textbf{\te{చలి}} and \textbf{\te{బాధ}} take the right-hand frame too.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item you are thirsty; ask for water
  \item it is cold today; then, it is very hot today
  \item tell a friend with a stomach ache to rest
  \item a friend says they are sad; react with \textquotedblleft{}really?\textquotedblright{}, then \textquotedblleft{}I see\textquotedblright{}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A fever? (\textbf{\te{జ్వరం}}.) A pain? (\textbf{\te{నొప్పి}}.) Tiredness? (\textbf{\te{అలసట}}.) Thirst? (\textbf{\te{దాహం}}.) Rest? (\textbf{\te{విశ్రాంతి}}.) Cold, and heat? (\textbf{\te{చలి}}, \textbf{\te{వేడి}}.) Fear, anger, sorrow? (\textbf{\te{భయం}}, \textbf{\te{కోపం}}, \textbf{\te{బాధ}}.) Really? (\textbf{\te{నిజంగా}}.) I see? (\textbf{\te{అలాగా}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
